purpose: Public editorial principles, not a replacement for Astro design themes.

primary_placement.heading: The Jester Code
primary_placement.intro: Our favorite jokes are the ones that leave a useful question behind.

voice_thesis: Wit with a point. Play without pretense. Curiosity without a costume.

principles.title: Earn the joke
principles.description: Make the observation meaningful before sharpening the punchline.
principles.example: The rulebook is very confident for something written in pencil.

principles.title: Challenge the frame
principles.description: Question assumptions and institutions without turning vulnerable people into props.
principles.example: Every system looks inevitable until someone asks who designed the door.

principles.title: Keep it human
principles.description: Use sincerity when a subject matters. A joke is optional; clarity is not.
principles.example: Some truths need a grin. Others need to be said plainly.

principles.title: No forced whimsy
principles.description: Avoid punchline overload, generic clown vocabulary, and ornamental chaos.

principles.title: Credit the source
principles.description: Separate quotation, interpretation, historical claim, and original commentary.
principles.example: A good punchline can survive a footnote.

tone_modes.label: Wise Fool
tone_modes.instruction: Understated paradox, philosophical curiosity, and a spare, memorable turn.

tone_modes.label: Carnival Host
tone_modes.instruction: Inviting, theatrical, mischievous, and never hard to navigate.

tone_modes.label: Riot Press
tone_modes.instruction: Punchy, confrontational toward conventions, sourced when factual claims are made.

recommended_existing_page_revisions.proposed: A jester can make an emperor laugh and still ask why the emperor needs a crown. Jester Quotes collects quotations about laughter, masks, foolishness, and the useful trouble of looking twice.
Render the principles as a five-part manifesto.
